newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Mobil urges Indonesia to boost incentives.
newsitem.headline: Mobil urges Indonesia to boost incentives.

text.p: Mobil Oil Corp chairman Lucio Noto on Tuesday urged Indonesia to give more incentives to boost oil and gas exploration and production.
"To maximise benefits in the future, we think there might be a few steps that the government should contemplate," Noto told the 25th annual convention of the Indonesian Petroleum Association.
Noto said Indonesia should accelerate the development of its domestic natural gas industry by creating a better regulatory framework and a more realistic pricing basis.
He said Jakarta should also extend exploration incentives in frontier areas.
Noto said he was grateful that Indonesia had improved its oil production sharing contract terms, but he noted the Indonesian government still took a relatively large share of profits.
"The minimum economic field size is still larger here than many other countries because of the total impact of tax and other financial incentives," he said.
"Overall, giving more incentives maximises the total benefit that comes from the opportunity," he said.
He said many countries from Latin America, Eastern Europe and the former Soviet Union were opening their doors by inviting international investors to participate in natural resource development.
"I think we all recognise that Indonesia should be doing everything it can to encourage the development of its remaining oil reserves," he said.

Indonesia's existing incentives are for exploration in high-risk frontier areas, including Irian Jaya, where contractors receive 35 percent of oil output from any find as opposed to 20 percent elsewhere in the archipelago.
Most of the world's major oil companies are engaged in exploration in Indonesia, including Mobil, Chevron Corp, Texaco Inc and Atlantic Richfield Co.
